THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
A chord's root and its bass note are **largely
key-independent**: both can be named correctly while the key label is wrong. So the root-agreement
percentage barely moves when the tonality is misread — while the chord's **quality**, its **Roman
numeral** and some of its **inversions** are all corrupted by that same misreading. The corpus
measurement therefore reports **less damage than a reader or listener would see**
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: A chord's root and its lowest note can both be named correctly while the key is wrong. So a measurement built on root agreement barely moves when the tonality is misread — but the quality of the chord, its Roman numeral and some of its inversions are all corrupted. The measurement therefore reports less damage than a listener or reader would see.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim records that a chord's root and bass are largely key-independent, so root agreement barely moves when the tonality is misread.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:

  was never executed on this path** — the production estimator replaced the pipeline instead — so

Two do not: they refine the reading from the notes alone and are not compensation for anything. Those two must be carried across, not deleted alongside the others.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **The perfect/imperfect cadence call is made on the BASS-DERIVED INVERSION; the soprano arrival

  confidence in a chordal texture; it never decides. *Why:* the constraint that forces it is the
  unavailability of the structural melody — orchestral doubling and a lead below the top are the two
  cited counter-cases — and the bass-derived inversion criterion is chosen because the catalog

Standard theory uses the melody note, but the program cannot reliably tell which line is the melody: the highest sounding voice is often a doubling, and in some music the lead sits below the top. THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: A user-facing preset presents as a familiar genre-era label plus exemplars the user knows — never as an idiom name or an obscure exemplar; genre names are LABELS over mixtures, never axes
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **A preset presents as a familiar genre-era label plus exemplars the user knows — never as an
  idiom name and never as an obscure exemplar; genre names are LABELS over mixtures, never axes.**
  A preset is named after a period and style a user recognises, anchored by musicians they know
  ("60s pop — The Beatles"); it is never named after one of the five idioms, and never after an
  exemplar most people have not heard of. *Why:* the second half is measured and is §6.7's own
  result — harmony is not organised by genre, and Baroque, galant and Classical share one idiom —
  so a genre name cannot be an axis without asserting a structure the data denies. The exemplar half
  is the user's own reason: an exemplar nobody recognises conveys nothing.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: What a user picks is named after a period and style they recognise, anchored by musicians they know. It is never named after one of the five structural idioms, and never after an exemplar most people have not heard of. The genre name is only a label for a blend of idioms — genre is not one of the things the analysis is organised by.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim presents a user-facing preset as a familiar genre-era label plus exemplars the user knows, never an idiom name.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on the style system's preset presentation, not on L3's facts.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: Preset coverage beyond the analysed corpora is three tiers with NO bare guessing — measured, editorially declared with a stated theory rationale, or self-correcting by detection
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **Coverage beyond the analysed music is three tiers with NO bare guessing — measured, editorially
  declared with a stated theory rationale, or self-correcting by detection.** A style we hold
  annotated music for gets its mixture measured from that music. A style we hold none for gets a
  mixture written down deliberately with its theory reason stated, and validated when data arrives.
  Either way the analysis moves away from the starting mixture as it reads the actual music. *Why:*
  the third tier is what licenses the second — because a preset is only a cold-start prior the music
  itself refines, a declared mixture that is somewhat wrong degrades gracefully; without the
  self-correction the declared tier would be an unvalidated shipped value (#19).
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: A style we hold annotated music for gets its blend measured from that music. A style we hold none for gets a blend written down deliberately, with the theory reason for it stated, and checked when data arrives. Either way the analysis moves away from the starting blend as it reads the actual score, so a badly chosen preset degrades gently rather than being wrong throughout.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim sets preset coverage in three tiers — measured, editorially declared, or self-correcting by detection.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on the style system, not on L3's five facts.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: Every idiom mixture is selectable and the discovered cloud is the EVIDENCE MAP, not the boundary — each chosen point carries its evidence status
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **Every idiom mixture is selectable, and the discovered cloud is the EVIDENCE MAP rather than the
  boundary — each chosen point carries its evidence status.** Named presets are cluster centroids
  for progressive disclosure; a custom selector admits any point in the mixture space. Where the
  chosen point sits relative to the music actually measured decides what may be claimed about it:
  inside a discovered cluster it is validated, between clusters it is an interpolation, outside the
  cloud it is still selectable but marked empirically unvalidated. *Why:* two standing rules
  combined — no information loss (#12), since restricting the user to the discovered centroids would
  discard every point between them, and the empirically-unvalidated mark, which lets a value outside
  the measured range be offered without being presented as established (#19).
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: A user may set any blend of the five idioms, not only the named ones. Where the chosen blend sits relative to the music we actually measured decides what may be claimed about it: inside a measured cluster it is validated, between clusters it is an interpolation, and outside everything measured it is still selectable but is marked as never having been checked against real music.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim makes every idiom mixture selectable, the discovered cloud being the evidence map rather than the boundary.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on the style system, not on L3's five facts.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: The score's own metadata is the PRIMARY home of that score's idiom mixture, and a user-set mixture is never silently overwritten by re-detection
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **The music's own metadata is the PRIMARY home of that piece's idiom mixture, and a user-set
  mixture is never silently overwritten by re-detection.** The mixture is stored in the score's own
  user-defined properties, the mechanism MuseScore already saves beside title and composer, so it
  travels with the file and a later analysis starts warm rather than cold. The stored value records
  its provenance — auto-detected, with the analyzer version and date, or user-set: a user-set
  mixture is never silently replaced, an auto-detected one may be refreshed, and an edit after
  detection marks the stored mixture refreshable. *Why:* storing it with the music removes the need
  for a separate registry for per-piece behaviour and turns re-analysis into a warm start; the
  no-silent-overwrite half is the no-surprise rule. **Two things are recorded rather than assumed
  away:** custom properties survive the native format but their MusicXML round-trip is only partial
  and needs its own check before the feature relies on it; and the property layout is an
  implementation decision at build time. **This sits against §13.1's rule that our data lives in
  separate files inside the archive and the score file is never touched** — the two are not in
  conflict on their own terms, since this uses MuseScore's existing property mechanism rather than
  extending the file's own schema, but a build must reconcile them explicitly and neither record
  does.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: A piece's blend of idioms is stored inside the piece's own file, using the score properties MuseScore already saves beside title and composer. So it travels with the file and a later analysis starts warm instead of cold. The stored value records whether a person set it or the program detected it: a person's setting is never quietly replaced, a detected one may be refreshed, and editing the score marks it as due for refresh.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim stores a piece's idiom mixture in the score's own metadata, a user-set mixture never silently overwritten by re-detection.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on where the style system stores its setting, not on L3's facts.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: The licence split for the style system: the ANCHORS are the shipped licence-constrained fitted parameters, and the mixture weights are free user configuration
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **The licence split: the ANCHORS are the shipped licence-constrained fitted parameters, and the
  mixture weights are free user configuration.** The constraint that a value which SHIPS may be
  fitted only on freely-licensed music reaches the per-idiom anchors, not the mixture a user chooses
  over them; a user's own mixture carries no constraint at all, and only the mixtures we ship as
  named preset defaults must be derived from a licensed pool or editorially declared. *Why:* it
  follows from what each half is — an anchor is a fitted parameter compiled into the product, so the
  fitting-pool constraint reaches it, while a mixture weight the user selects is configuration
  derived from no corpus at all. This REFINES the fitting-pool constraint by saying which half of
  the style system it reaches; it does not weaken it.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: The licensing rule that limits which music our shipped numbers may be fitted on applies to the per-idiom reference values, not to the blend a user chooses over them. A user's own blend carries no constraint at all; only the blends we ship as named defaults must come from freely-licensed music or be declared editorially.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim puts the licence constraint on the per-idiom anchors and leaves the mixture weights free user configuration.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on licensing within the style system, not on L3's facts.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: The style taxonomy and the per-style weights are ONE data-derived object; VALIDATION is a separate third thing that needs annotated scores and is not delivered by the clustering
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **The taxonomy and the per-style weights are ONE data-derived object; VALIDATION is a separate
  third thing the clustering does not deliver.** Discovering which idioms exist and estimating how
  strongly each one weighs are not two derivations: the clusters and their feature distributions
  are the same object read two ways. Measuring whether the analysis actually improves when it uses
  an idiom is a THIRD job, and it needs annotated music — notes together with a published human
  analysis — which the clustering does not supply. *Why:* it follows from what a cluster is, so no
  second derivation produces the weights; and the separation is forced by what validation measures,
  the analysis's USE of an idiom, which cannot be observed without a human analysis to compare
  against.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: Discovering which styles exist and measuring how strongly each one weighs are not two jobs — they are the clusters and their distributions, one result. Checking whether the analysis actually gets better when it uses a style is a third, separate job, and it needs music with both the notes and a published human analysis, which the clustering does not supply.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim makes the taxonomy and the per-style weights one data-derived object, with validation a separate third thing.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on the style taxonomy's method, not on L3's five facts.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: The quality-overwrite information-loss violation is TOLERATED until the gate-dissolution step and stays VISIBLE in the open-items register — tolerated is not forgotten
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
Two post-scoring passes change the chord quality the scorer committed and keep no record of what
they replaced, which is an information-loss violation (#12). **The verdict is to TOLERATE it until
the gate-dissolution step, with the violation kept VISIBLE in the open-items register — tolerated is
not forgotten.** *Why, as a derivation from three principles rather than a preference:* removing the
overwrites now would be a production behaviour change with no replacement owner, since no component
yet owns deciding quality from the key — which is the cross-layer patch layer adherence forbids
(#7); and #8 puts the structural work first. Deferring to the step that gives the concern a single
home makes the removal ONE ratified, revertible change under the regression stop (#14/#15). The
alternative — ripping the overwrites out now — was considered and rejected on exactly that ground.
**The open-items register row is the mechanism that makes this an acceptance rather than an
oversight**, and it gates the dissolution.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: Two later passes change the chord quality the chord stage committed and keep no record of what they replaced, which is information loss. It is left in place for now rather than ripped out, because there is no other component yet that owns deciding quality from the key, and removing it now would be a patch across stages. The violation is kept on the open-items list so that leaving it is a decision and not an oversight.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim tolerates two post-scoring passes that overwrite the committed chord quality, kept visible in the open-items register until the gate-dissolution step.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on how the chord quality is decided, which is L2's.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: Before any constant that would make two differently-scaled confidences comparable is fitted, the premise that a fitted constant CAN do so must itself pass a premise ledger and a desk simulation
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
The `conversion`
element of a frame is where two numbers on different scales are made comparable — one bounded, one an unbounded
sum — and fitting the constants that perform it is **hard-gated**: the premise *"a fitted constant CAN make these
scales commensurable"* is itself a load-bearing causal claim and goes through the #17 ledger and desk simulation
BEFORE the fit, not as part of it.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: Two confidence numbers in the program are on different scales — one runs from zero to one, the other is an unbounded total — and a comparison between them treats them as the same kind of quantity. Fitting a conversion factor is not allowed to be the first move: the assumption that any single factor could make the two comparable has to be written down as a premise and traced by hand first, because the one attempt at such a calibration did not behave monotonically.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim hard-gates fitting a frame's conversion constant behind a premise ledger and a desk simulation.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It belongs to the confidence contract and names none of L3's facts.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: The local-key hypothesis derives from key-agnostic signals ONLY and never from the key-area grouping, which is a post-grouping of the resolved key — a hard design rule, not a preference
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **A local-key hypothesis derives from KEY-AGNOSTIC signals only, and NEVER from the key-area
  grouping — a hard design rule, not a preference.** Deciding that a passage has moved to another
  key may use the cadence detector, which is key-agnostic by construction, and the raw region
  structure — root motion, diatonic-collection consistency. It may **not** read the key-area
  grouping, which is a downstream post-grouping of the already-resolved key. The flow stays
  strictly feed-forward: chords → key-agnostic cadence → local-key hypothesis → re-keyed key path →
  key areas, rebuilt downstream. *Why:* named in the decision as the load-bearing soundness
  property, and the circularity is concrete rather than argued — the grouping is built FROM the
  resolved key, so a detector reading it would find the key it was given. It is the same discipline
  that made the cadence detector usable, applied to the local-key hypothesis and naming the exact
  surface that would make it circular. **Scope:** the mechanism this rule was written for sits on
  the legacy key path, but what it constrains is *what evidence a modulation decision may read*,
  which binds any such decision on any arm.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: Deciding that a passage has moved to a new key may only use evidence that does not already assume a key: the closure detector, which works without being told the key, and the plain shape of the music. It may not read the key-area grouping, because that grouping is built FROM the key already decided — using it would mean the detector confirming its own input.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim rules that a local-key hypothesis derives from key-agnostic signals only — the cadence detector and the raw region structure — and never from the key-area grouping.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: Ruled IN 2026-10-15 from OUT (Ruling 2 of `cowork_rulings_2026_10_15_l3_withheld_family_lists_sitting.md`): its subject is L2's decision, but its published text states in passing that cadences are detected without the key and from the decided chords, which is the core of D-336, withheld by Ruling 1; admitted beside it, this entry would carry that answer into the pack without citing D-336, and withholding it costs the deriving session nothing it needs, L3 receiving the tonality settled.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: Ground truth for IMPLIED polyphony is confirmed ABSENT — do not re-search it
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
**Negatives (do not re-search):** implied-polyphony GT over monophonic instruments — CONFIRMED ABSENT
(VoiSe 2005 and Gray & Bunescu's perceptual-stream pop corpus were never released; VISA excerpt sets not
public; Chew&Wu/Guiomard-Kagan reused notated voices).
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: For music where several lines are implied by a single melodic instrument, no published collection of correct line assignments exists — every candidate was either never released or simply reuses the voices the engraver wrote. The absence is the finding, and the record says so rather than leaving the search open.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim records ground truth for implied polyphony confirmed absent.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on corpus search.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: Every real difficulty-grade label source is research-only or proprietary at origin — a commercial grading feature needs a licence path or its own labels
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
**★ AND THE DIFFICULTY-GRADE CASE IS A DIFFERENT PROHIBITION FROM THE FOUR BULLETS ABOVE, STATED APART SO IT IS NOT
READ AS THE SAME ONE.** Those restrict the pool a **shipped FITTED VALUE** may be estimated on. This restricts a
shipped **FEATURE** whose labels are somebody else's property. **Every real difficulty-grade label source is
research-only or proprietary AT ORIGIN:** no machine-readable exam-syllabus dump exists in any form, the open sets
carry no licence file at all, the gated one is request-access and research-use-only, and the largest carries a
free-licence badge over research-use-only text. **So a COMMERCIAL grading feature needs a licence path or labels of
our own** — the held material is enough to validate the idea as research and is not enough to ship it. *Why it is
stated here and not only where it was found:* this is the section a fitter or a feature design reads before declaring
its pool, and a designer who meets the fitted-value rule must also meet the case where the constraint bites on the
feature instead.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: Every collection that says how hard a piece is to play is either restricted to research use or belongs to somebody who sells it. So a difficulty feature in a shipped product would need either a licence agreement or labels of our own; the held material is enough to check the idea works and not enough to ship it.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim records every difficulty-grade label source research-only or proprietary at origin.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It is licensing.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: A global tonic anchor enters key scoring at RESOLVER/SECTION scope — never as one more local term inside the window scorer, which is what re-enters the coupling that defeated the local levers
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **A global tonic anchor enters key scoring at RESOLVER / SECTION scope — never as one more local
  term inside the window scorer. ⚠ LEGACY: both mechanisms it names are legacy-scoped.** Evidence
  about which key a whole section or piece is in is applied where the section is decided — the
  scope the removed declared anchor occupied — gating the relative-major/minor choice; the
  per-window candidate scoring is left unchanged. *Why:* measured, at the attempt that failed —
  local reweighting was shown unable to carry the relative-major/minor decision, because that floor
  is made of near-ties and any local term strong enough to win them without the mode present also
  overrides the correct reading when it is present. Adding the anchor as one more local term
  re-enters exactly that coupling. The design attaches a proof obligation to the rule: show that
  the anchor reinforces the mode-present cases rather than regressing them. **The LEGACY mark
  follows a check at the code, not the decision's age:** the window scorer this rule excludes
  (`KeyModeAnalyzer::analyzeKeyMode`) is reached only through the legacy resolver and this layer's
  dormant sequence decoder, and the resolver is retired from the production region path — so
  neither named mechanism is on an arm that runs. The rule about WHERE a section-scoped prior is
  applied binds any such prior the key axis later gains.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: Evidence about which key a whole passage is in is applied where the passage is decided, not inside the per-window scoring that ranks candidate keys note by note. Adding it as one more local term is what failed before: any local term strong enough to settle a near-tie when the mode is unknown also overrides the correct answer when the mode IS known.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim applies a global tonic anchor at resolver or section scope, never as a local term inside the window scorer.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on the tonality decision, which is L2's.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: The reach-back convergence PROXY was measured FALSE and dropped — the as-built tracks the leading-edge key itself and stops when it stops changing
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **The reach-back convergence PROXY was measured FALSE and is dropped; the as-built tracks the
  leading-edge key itself and stops when that stops changing.** The cheaper stopping rule proposed
  in design — *a settled, stable prevailing key is in view in the reached-back region* — was
  measured and disproved: one settled indication of context does not anchor the leading edge, which flips
  only once a confident earlier key is established over a **run**. So the facility uses the
  headline criterion directly and no proxy. *Why:* measured at the build, and the methodological
  reading is recorded with the result — the proxy was an unlabelled assumption, it was measured, it
  was false, and it was dropped; a determinism test over extension step size is what validates the
  criterion that replaced it. This is the finding that supersedes the proxy clause of the
  bounded-context contract's convergence item; that contract now records the clause as tried and
  closed, and its headline rule — reach back until the answer stops changing, never by a chosen
  amount — is unchanged.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: When the analysis has to read backwards for context, it needs a rule for when it has read far enough. The cheap rule proposed in design — stop once a settled key appears anywhere in the material read back — was measured and found to stop too early: one settled measure does not fix the key at the edge of the selection, which only settles once a confident earlier key is established over a stretch. So the built code checks the thing that actually matters and stops when that stops moving.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim records the reach-back convergence proxy measured false and dropped, the as-built tracking the leading-edge key until it stops changing.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on the tonality decision's context extension, which is L2's and the bounded context's.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: A selection-aware capability is a PARAMETER on the one orchestrator, never a sibling — the capability must not duplicate the orchestration
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
**A selection-aware capability is a PARAMETER on the one orchestrator, never a sibling (D-623;
re-homed into this specification 2026-08-04, from the same document as D-624).** The capability was built as an option on the existing
driver rather than as a second driver beside it, so there remains **one** path that builds the note
model, slices it and decodes — the seam specified below. The option is off by default, so shipped
behaviour and every measurement are unchanged. *Why:* it is one-path-per-concern applied to
orchestration — a second driver would be a second place where build, slice and decode are sequenced,
and the two would drift. Both admissible forms were stated, and the build's choice was gated on
byte-identity plus an explicit unification ledger, so the resolution is evidenced rather than asserted.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: A new way of driving the analysis over part of a score was built as an option on the existing driver rather than as a second driver beside it, so there is still one path that builds the note model, cuts it into slices and decodes them. The option is off by default, so the shipped behaviour and every measurement are unchanged.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim makes a selection-aware capability a parameter on the one orchestrator, never a sibling.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It is code structure.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: Spelling presence is tested with the validity predicate, never with a non-negative test — the flat side of the line of fifths is negative and a non-negative guard silently drops it
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
- **Spelling presence is tested with the VALIDITY PREDICATE, never with a non-negative test.** The
  shared line-of-fifths primitive the spelling-pin above reads — the one interpreter, not a
  per-layer copy — represents a spelling as a signed position on the line of fifths, and its
  presence test is `tpcIsValid()`, **never** `tpc >= 0` and never `tpc != -1`. *Why:* established
  at the source rather than asserted — the flat side of the line of fifths is **negative** (down to
  the triple-flat spellings), so a non-negative guard silently discards every heavily flattened
  spelling; and the value a `!= -1` guard treats as absent is itself a **legitimate** spelling. The
  honest bound is recorded with the rule: the validity test cannot tell a real flattest spelling
  from a default-initialised field, and what actually keeps an absent value out is the build-path
  invariant, not this predicate. §5.14, which specifies the enharmonic disambiguation this
  primitive serves, points here and does not restate it (#6).
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: How a note is spelt is stored as a position on the line of fifths, and that position is negative for the flattest spellings. Code that checks whether a spelling is present by testing for a non-negative number therefore throws away every heavily-flattened spelling — including one that happens to share its number with the field's empty value. The validity test is the correct check.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim rules spelling presence tested with the validity predicate `tpcIsValid()`, never with a non-negative test.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on the note reader's spelling primitive (L0), not on how any of L3's facts is read off.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: The resolver of carried uncertain readings IS the function layer itself — there is no distinct gated box between the note layers and it
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
**★ THE RESOLVER OF CARRIED UNCERTAIN READINGS IS THIS LAYER ITSELF — THERE IS NO DISTINCT GATED BOX
BETWEEN THE NOTE LAYERS AND IT (re-homed into this specification 2026-08-08 on the user's ruling).**
When the earlier layers cannot decide between two readings they carry both forward with an
uncertainty mark. **What resolves them is this layer, as part of assigning function**: it reads the
carried alternatives and the marks at its gated entry, assigns function under each carried
key/chord reading, and keeps the reading whose functional and cadential analysis is coherent. The
"gated step" language elsewhere in the specifications describes **this layer's gated entry**, not a
separate layer.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: When the earlier stages cannot decide between two readings they hand both forward with a mark. The thing that then picks one is not a separate component: it is the function stage, choosing as part of naming the harmony. The wording elsewhere about a gated step describes the point at which that stage begins, not another stage.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim makes the function layer itself the resolver of carried uncertain readings, with no distinct gated box.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on how carried key and chord readings are settled, which is L2's decision.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: The crediting rule is NOT amended to count a tonicization label as agreeing with the annotator's modulated numeral; only a diagnostic partial-sub-split is defensible
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
**★ THE CREDITING RULE IS NOT AMENDED TO COUNT A TONICIZATION LABEL AS AGREEING WITH THE
ANNOTATOR'S MODULATED NUMERAL; ONLY A DIAGNOSTIC PARTIAL-SUB-SPLIT IS DEFENSIBLE** (2026-06-14; the
record states no ratifier for the decision itself. Homed here 2026-08-09 on the user's ruling —
Ruling 11 of `records/cowork/rulings/cowork_rulings_2026_08_09_second_stop.md` — as the MEASUREMENT half of register entry
**D-291**, whose BUILD half belongs to the Layer-5 function specification and is not restated here,
#6. **SPLIT INTO TWO REGISTER IDENTIFIERS 2026-08-09** on the user's Ruling 21 of
`records/cowork/rulings/cowork_rulings_2026_08_09_fourth_stop.md`: this half now carries its own entry, **D-656**, and
**D-291** keeps the build half; the two cross-reference each other, and neither text changed).
Where our analysis labels an applied chord relative to the home key and the human annotator
has changed key, the comparison is **not** to be changed so that the label counts as agreement.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: Where our analysis names an applied chord relative to the home key and the human annotator has changed key, the accuracy comparison is not to be altered so that our label counts as agreeing. Only a diagnostic that splits such cases out and exposes the masking is defensible. This is the measurement half of a decision whose build half — leaving the labeller unwired — belongs to the function layer's specification.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim forbids amending the crediting rule to count a tonicization label as agreeing with the annotator's modulated numeral.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on the measurement of the analysis, not on L3's five facts.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: A research-tied name is not renamed but is governed by a two-tier rule, and the terminology cleanup runs in a fixed order with no tree-wide rename
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
**★ WHAT HAPPENS TO A NAME BORROWED FROM THE PUBLISHED RESEARCH, AND IN WHAT ORDER THE CLEANUP
  RUNS (user-ruled 2026-08-09; the ruling record is `records/cowork/rulings/cowork_rulings_2026_08_09_fifth_stop.md`,
  Ruling 30).** The block above says the existing tree is not renamed unilaterally and that the
  pass is a decision surface rather than a sweep. It does not say what a session does with a term
  that carries correspondence to the research the design is grounded in, and it does not fix the
  order — both are settled here. **A RESEARCH-TIED NAME IS NOT RENAMED (#1/#2), AND IS GOVERNED BY
  TWO TIERS.** *(i)* At the **INTRODUCTION SITE** — where the public research is actually
  discussed, which is expected to be one or very few places — the collision is EXPLAINED and our
  decided synonym STATED; the term standing there with that statement is conformant. *(ii)* **Every
  subsequent use** of the research term outside our own vocabulary carries a **compact inline
  annotation referencing the research**; such a use is conformant if and only if it is annotated,
  and an **unannotated repeat use is a flag**.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: A term borrowed from the published research that collides with this project's vocabulary is not renamed. Instead: where the research is actually discussed, the collision is explained and our own synonym stated; and every later use of the borrowed term outside our vocabulary carries a short inline note pointing at the research, so an unannotated repeat use is a flag. The wider terminology cleanup runs in a fixed order — the derived inventory first, then per-word batches the user rules, governing surfaces first — and there is no tree-wide rename.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim governs a research-tied name by a two-tier annotation rule, with no tree-wide rename.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It is documentation governance.

THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.title: What a voice/stream label set actually MEASURES is said at intake — the labels obtainable today come from engraved notation, not from a listener's judgment
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.verbatim:
4. **What a voice/stream label set actually MEASURES is said at intake** (user-ruled 2026-08-09) — the
   voice labels obtainable today are derived from **engraved notation**, not from a listener's
   judgment about heard lines, and the intake record says so in those terms.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.plain: When a collection of per-note voice labels is taken in, the record states where those labels came from: they are read off the way the music was written down, not off what a listener hears as separate lines. For keyboard music the two are close enough that the field works with the engraved version, and that acceptance is recorded too rather than left unsaid.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.finding: Its verbatim requires an intake record to say that voice labels come from engraved notation, not from a listener's judgment.
THE_CANDIDATES_AND_THEIR_VERDICTS.reason: It bears on corpus intake for the voice-leading axis.

filters_applied.heading_contains: detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

filters_applied.the_text_removed:
## What an L3 detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

*(The L3 charter, `FRAMEWORK.md` §5 "L3 — The read-off facts": L3 answers "given a settled tonal reading,
what else does a harmonic analysis of this music say?", consumes L2's published facts plus L0's and L1's,
may not revise L2, and publishes, among other facts, "the figured bass".)*

- **Adopt — the equivalence rules of §3.2.2 as the grading rule for any figured bass L3 publishes.** They
  are stated, sourced to Arnold, and they move the simple algorithm from a 3% exact match to 64.5%. A
  measurement of L3's figured bass against Bach's figures would need them or rules doing the same work.
- **Adopt — the unit: a figure is the set of intervals above the bass in one slice, with the score's
  spelling deciding the number and accidental.** That is what a figured bass is in this ground truth.
- **Must argue against, or at least answer — the placement.** The paper produces figured bass **from the
  notes alone, with no chord and no key**, and its §5 proposes the reverse of L3's order: figured bass
  first, chord labels from it. Under consequence (i) of `reading_pass/candidacy_upgrades.md`'s criterion,
  a method the chosen placement excludes is a candidate and the specification must carry the exclusion.
  The L3 charter places figured bass after the settled tonal reading. The paper does not measure a
  chord-based alternative, so it neither supports nor contradicts that placement; it is the
  **rival-shaped** upstream route, and the L3 specification owes a sentence saying why it is not taken.
- **Adapt — what a figured bass read off settled chords would miss.** Bach's figures often carry
  suspension figures (the paper's examples are 4–3 and 9–8; the equivalence rules also name 6–5), though
  he *"sometimes omitted them"* (§4); and the authors' rule (2) removes ornamental notes from the figure
  to come closer to his figures. A figured bass computed only from a decided chord and its inversion would
  not produce the suspension figures. **This side's reading: L3's figured bass would need L2's published
  elaboration relations (which notes are suspensions, passing tones and so on) as well as the chord**, if
  it is meant to agree with this ground truth. Whether L2 publishes enough for that is a question for the
  L3 derivation, not answered here.

filters_applied.the_text_removed:
## ★ Findings, routed and not applied

**(1) A statement in `FRAMEWORK.md` pairs this paper's figures wrongly.** `FRAMEWORK.md` Appendix B, §S2
(the first-stage draft, kept whole and unedited), says: *"a rule-based labeller matches his figures
exactly 3% of the time and 85.3% under a music-theoretic equivalence metric — the gap is notation
convention, not analysis."* At the paper: the **3%** is the **simple** rule-based algorithm's exact match
(642); the same simple algorithm under the equivalence metric scores **64.5%** (643); the **85.3%** is
the **improved** algorithm, after two added rules, one of which removes passing tones, neighbour tones,
escape tones and anticipations (643). So the 3%-to-85.3% gap is **not** one labeller under two metrics,
and part of it comes from an analytical step (finding ornamental notes), not from notation convention.
The paper does not say "the gap is notation convention". **Each number is printed in the paper; the
pairing and the conclusion drawn from it are not.** *Where it sits:* Appendix B is the sealed first-stage
draft, and the main body's R-1 cites figured bass only as a source of an agreement figure, which stands.
This side found no CHOSEN design point whose defense rests on the sentence, from the searched lines only
(a search of `FRAMEWORK.md` for "figured bass" and its variants); it has not established that none does.
**Routed to the user as a finding of its own; nothing is amended.**

**(2) The 85.3% is a figure the rules were selected against** (footnote 20). Any later use of it as a
measured accuracy carries that qualification (principle #20). The cross-validated figures are 84.3% and
85.9%.

**(3) BCFB is a figured-bass ground truth on Bach chorales.** Routed to measurement design and to the
corpus needs list. **Not checked:** whether BCFB is held in this repository, and which of its chorales
overlap the regression corpus. If they overlap, `D-514` (an annotation set whose works overlap the
regression corpus is record-only without a user ruling) would apply; this side has not established the
overlap.

**(4) The paper's slice is not this project's slice.** The paper cuts a new slice at every note
**onset** only (§3.2.1); this project's slice (`DECISIONS.md` terms table) begins when any note starts
**or stops**. Recorded for any L3 derivation that would compare against BCFB slice by slice.

**(5) No falsifier.** Nothing read contradicts any CHOSEN design point. The paper's upstream route is
rival-shaped against the L3 placement, as stated above, and measures nothing against it. **No STOP
fires** under the commission's §6 on this paper's content; finding (1) is a wrong citation in the
framework's sealed appendix, put to the user on its own.

filters_applied.the_text_removed:
## What an L1 detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

- **Adopt — the three-onset frame (X, Y, Z) as the shape of a local cue.** A cue is not a property of one
  moment but of an arrival and its named preparation, and the paper's own ablation shows the preparation
  earns its place: dropping X and Y (feature set ZR) costs 0.80 → 0.52 on Bach PAC.
- **Adopt — the bass-implied-tonality construction.** `Z-bass-compatible-with-I` is a *hypothetical*
  tonality anchored on the bass of the arrival, tested by the presence of degrees 4 and 7 in the
  preceding beats. **This is exactly what lets a cue be key-agnostic without being tonality-blind**, and
  it is the construction the L1 charter's third cue names.
- **Adapt — the metric-strength cue as a filter rather than as evidence.** `R-Z-strong-beat` *"correctly
  filters out more than half of the beats"*, which is a different role from contributing weight.
- **Must argue against — nothing here.** The paper is not a rival to any chosen point; it is the primary
  under one.

filters_applied.heading_contains: ★ Findings, routed and not applied
filters_applied.why: Limb A of Ruling 1 of 2026-09-21: project-facing text (`reading_pass/l3_extracts_per_file_cut_list_2026_10_16.md`, §4, this file)
filters_applied.the_text_removed:
## ★ Findings, routed and not applied

**(1) The L1 charter's cadence-cue paragraph verifies at this primary, in three separate places.** The
charter says the cues are *"computable from the notation without knowing the tonality"* — §2.1 says the
authors do not perform tonality estimation, and §1.3/§2 say they avoid chord segmentation and harmonic
analysis. The charter says *"hand-designed local features reach F .80 on perfect authentic cadences
with, in the authors' words, no chord segmentation and no tonality estimation"* — Table 3, bach-wtc-i
PAC, F₁ **0.80**. The charter says the half cadence is weak *"because the bass motion into a half cadence
is variable"* — §4.2 in the authors' own words. **No correction is owed on any of the three.**

**(2) The framework's third cue is this paper's feature, and the precision is worth carrying into the
detail specification.** The charter's *"the sounding together of the fourth and seventh degrees of a
candidate tonality in the approach"* is `Z-bass-compatible-with-I`: degrees 4 and 7 **of the tonality
implied by the bass of the arrival chord**, present **in the four beats before it**. The phrase
*candidate tonality* is therefore not loose — it names a hypothesis anchored on a note the score gives,
which is what keeps the cue inside L1's *decides nothing* rule. **Recorded for the derivation; nothing
is amended.**

**(3) A caution the charter does not carry, and a derivation should.** The Haydn cadence annotations
this study is graded against *"model cadences in the light of a global analysis of the form"* while the
detection is local, and the authors say at least five of the twenty-eight Haydn PAC false positives
*"can be seen as actual cadences"*. **The ceiling on a local cue is partly an artefact of a
form-level ground truth** — principle #21's shape, on the cadence axis. **Routed to measurement design.**

**(4) No falsifier.** Nothing read contradicts any CHOSEN design point. **No STOP fires** under the
remedial commission's §5.

filters_applied.heading_contains: detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

filters_applied.the_text_removed:
## What an L1 detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

- **Adopt as evidence, not as machinery — the granularity result.** A cadence cue can be carried at the
  **note** level and aggregated upward. In Tables 2 and 4 the note-level figure is the highest of the
  three in every row that reports it; **Table 3 prints the note-level macro F1 below the beat-level one
  in five of its six cells** (p. 6). Our L1 publishes cues per change point; on Tables 2 and 4 this is
  measured support that the finer grain is not a loss.
  *(★ CORRECTED 2026-09-20 ON THE USER'S RULING. Former wording, preserved (#12): "and the note-level
  figures are consistently the highest of the three. Our L1 publishes cues per change point; this is
  measured support that the finer grain is not a loss.")*
- **Adapt — the finding that local features plus non-local structure beat local features alone.** The
  paper's measurement of the graph's contribution is Table 4 — PAC in the Bach fugues only, one value per
  depth, no spread printed: depth 2 gives the highest figure at all three levels, and no convolution
  the lowest at note and onset level (p. 6). Table 3 does not measure it: both of its arms carry the
  graph convolution and neither carries [4]'s anchor heuristics; that the general features' performance
  *"implies"* graph-supplied context is the authors' reading (p. 6).
  *(★ CORRECTED 2026-09-20 ON THE USER'S RULING. Former wording, preserved (#12): "The general-feature
  arm of Table 3 shows a graph's neighbourhood supplies context that hand-designed anchor heuristics
  were previously carrying.")* **For L1 this is a caution rather than a design**: L1 decides
  nothing, so it may publish cues but must not acquire a learned context stage of its own — that context
  belongs to L2, which sees the whole span.
- **Must argue against — nothing here.** Like row 37, this is a primary under a chosen point, not a rival
  to one.

filters_applied.the_text_removed:
## ★ Findings, routed and not applied

**(1) ★ THE FRAMEWORK'S ".29 AND .41" PAIR IS VERIFIED, AND BOTH VALUES SIT IN THIS ONE TABLE.** The L1
charter carries: *"the half cadence reaches F .29 and .41 in those same two studies."* Table 2 of this
paper reports **0.29** for the Bigo et al. reference model on Haydn HC — the same value row 37's own
Table 3 reports — and **0.41** for this paper's own pretrained model on the same target. **Both halves of
the charter's figure verify at the object, and the two studies are now both read whole. No correction is
owed.**

**(2) The agreement the charter's DP-I rests on is real, and it is two methods on shared data.** *"our
results agree with [4] in implying that half cadences (HC) seem significantly harder to identify than
authentic cadences"* — a different method, on *"two datasets also used by Bigo et al. [4]"* (p. 3) with
*"the same data and train/test setup"* (p. 4); the Haydn half-cadence comparison is on the Haydn corpus
annotated by *"Sears and colleagues [19]"* (p. 3), and [4]'s figures are *"taken from [4]"* (p. 5).
**DP-I's split — cues at L1, type at L3 — is supported by two primaries rather than one, and both are
now at the object; their methods differ, their Haydn corpus and its annotations are shared.**
*(★ CORRECTED 2026-09-20 ON THE USER'S RULING. Former wording, preserved (#12): the heading "The
independent replication the charter's DP-I rests on is real and is stated as such."; the quotation
without "(HC)"; "— an independent method, a different corpus, the same conclusion."; and the closing
sentence without its last clause.)*

**(3) ★ A finding that sharpens what the charter means by a cue, and that the derivation should carry.**
This paper deliberately **removed** row 37's anchor-point heuristics and still reached comparable results
by letting a graph supply the surrounding context. Read together, the two papers say the cue is carried
by **local musical evidence plus some view of its surroundings**, and that the surroundings can be
supplied either by hand-named anchors or learned. **For L1 that is a boundary statement, not a licence:**
the charter has L1 publish evidence at change points and decide nothing, so the surrounding-context half
belongs to the layer that sees the span. **Routed to the L1 and L2 detail specifications; nothing is
amended.**
*(★ NOTE 2026-09-20 ON THE USER'S RULING: "comparable" is the paper's own word, and "by letting a graph
supply the surrounding context" is the paper's own attribution — its "implies", read off Table 3
(p. 6). The page's measurement of the graph's contribution is Table 4, at the scope the "Adapt"
verdict above states. The finding's text is otherwise unchanged.)*

**(4) A ceiling caution, agreeing with row 37's from the other side.** Row 37 records that at least five
of its Haydn PAC false positives *"can be seen as actual cadences"*. This paper's §6.2 says the same in
its own words and works an example: cadential patterns inside a modulating sequence, textbook-correct at
the arrival, counted as false positives because whether they are cadences *"is a matter of higher-level
musicological considerations."* **Two studies — different methods, the same Haydn annotations by
Sears and colleagues [19] (p. 3) — report that the annotation, not only the method, bounds the
measured figure.** *(★ CORRECTED 2026-09-20 ON THE USER'S RULING. Former wording, preserved (#12): "Two
independent studies report that the annotation, not only the method, bounds the measured figure.")*
Principle #21's shape on the cadence axis. **Routed to measurement design.**

**(5) No falsifier.** Nothing read contradicts any CHOSEN design point. **No STOP fires** under the
remedial commission's §5.

## ★ The doubt-default question, answered

**Its method does NOT bear on L1's cues. It bears on perception, and — secondarily — on how a cadence
ground truth and a cadence measurement are read.** Three findings at the object settle it, and any one
of them would:

1. **It does not detect cadences. It consumes them.** The cadence collection is **annotated by hand**
   under Caplin's typology and supplied to the analysis; the study then measures how *predictable* the
   annotated terminal events are. A detection task, a classifier, a precision or a recall is met nowhere
   in the paper's pages as read. *(★ CORRECTED 2026-10-15 at the cross-check, as an absolute narrowed to
   what a read establishes. FORMER WORDING, PRESERVED (#12): "There is no detection task, no classifier,
   no precision and no recall anywhere in the paper." Both reads found none; the fact is unchanged.)*
2. **★ Its harmonic viewpoints require a hand-annotated tonality.** [FACT, §5.2] *"to relate `cpitch`
   to a referential tonic pitch class for every event in the corpus, we manually annotated the key,
   mode, modulations and pivot boundaries for each movement."* **The scale-degree viewpoints `csd` and
   `csdc` are computed from a key that a human supplied; the third harmonic viewpoint, `vintcc`, is not —
   it encodes intervals above the lowest part, modulo 12 (§5.2.2, p. 10) — and it carries results in
   Tables 4 to 7 beside `csdc`.** *(★ CORRECTED 2026-10-15 at the cross-check. FORMER WORDING, PRESERVED
   (#12): "**The scale-degree viewpoints `csd` and `csdc` — the ones carrying every harmonic result in the
   paper — are computed from a key that a human supplied.**" `vintcc` is a harmonic viewpoint that needs
   no key.)* A method that consumes a decided tonality cannot produce an L1 cue, L1 being the layer
   that decides nothing and runs before any tonality exists. *(The conclusion still holds through `csd`,
   `csdc`, `composite` and the hand-annotated cadence collection of item 1.)*
3. **The authors name their own object of study, in the paper's last sentence.** [FACT, §7] *"the
   schematic expectations formed by listeners for cadences and other recurrent temporal patterns amount
   to these sorts of probabilistic inferences requires an entirely different approach, one in which the
   listener, rather than the music, represents the primary object of study."*

**So the doubt resolves against L1 candidacy — and the reading was still worth its cost**, because three
of its findings bear on things the record does care about. Those are §"Findings" below.

## ★ Findings, routed and not applied

**(1) ★ A THIRD INDEPENDENT STATEMENT THAT THE HALF CADENCE IS NOT SEPARABLE BY LOCAL EVIDENCE — AND IT
COMES FROM A DIFFERENT KIND OF METHOD ENTIRELY.** Rows 37 and 38 say it in F-measure (0.29 and 0.41
against 0.80 for the perfect authentic cadence). This study says it in information content: the terminal
events of a half cadence are *"no more (or less) predictable than any other instance of root-position
dominant harmony selected at random from the corpus."* **Detection and predictability are different
measurements, and they agree.** This strengthens DP-I's recorded ground — cues at L1, type at L3 —
beyond what the charter currently cites. **Routed as an addition candidate to DP-I's defense; not
applied, an amendment being the user's act on a surface.**
*(★ BOUND ADDED 2026-10-15 AT THE CROSS-CHECK; the wording above is left as written (#12). At the paper
(Table 5, p. 14; p. 12) the quoted sentence holds for the cello and the three chord viewpoints and does
NOT hold for the first violin under `cpitch`, `melint` and `selection`, where the half cadence's terminal
events were significantly more predictable than random root-position dominants. So a citation of it
carries that viewpoint bound. And the paper measures group-mean predictability from preceding context,
not separability: a classification of half cadences against other dominants is met nowhere in its pages
as read. Whether the finding therefore strengthens DP-I's ground, as written above, or bears on it only
indirectly, as the second extraction reads it, is a difference of reading the two extracts do not
resolve; it is left to the L3 specification's author.)*

**(2) ★ A PRECISION ABOUT THE "TWO INDEPENDENT STUDIES", worth carrying because a later reader will lean
on it.** The L1 charter cites rows 37 and 38 as two independent studies. **They are independent in
METHOD and not in DATA:** row 38 states it uses *"two datasets also used by Bigo et al."*, and row 37's
Haydn cadence annotations are *"from Sears and colleagues"* — that is, from **this paper's own author
group and annotation programme**. So the replication is a second method over largely the same annotated
material. **The charter's sentence is not wrong** — they are two studies and they are independent — **but
the independence does not extend to the ground truth, and a derivation that leans on the replication
should say which kind of independence it is relying on.** *(Finding (1) is not subject to this caveat in
the same way: it is a third method AND a different measurement, though on the same composer.)*
**Recorded; nothing amended.**

**(3) ★ A FINDING ABOUT BASS EVIDENCE THAT BEARS ON HOW ANY CUE IS FORMED.** In isolation, the cadential
bass leap is *less* predictable than the stepwise motion of non-cadential contexts — so a single-voice
statistical model **penalises exactly the motion that signals the cadence**, and the sign of the effect
reverses. Only viewpoints that model the interaction between bass and upper voices recover the expected
direction. **The practical statement for a detail specification: a cue defined over the bass alone can
have the wrong sign; the cue is the bass motion IN RELATION to what sounds above it.** *(Read beside row
37, which reaches the same place from the other side: its bass-move features are always relative to the
chord at the arrival, never to the bass line alone.)* **Routed to the L1 and L2 detail specifications.**

**(4) A boundary-evidence claim, routed to the phrase-boundary primitive and to L3, not to L1.**
Experiment 3's result is that a boundary's strength lies partly in the **rise** in information content
*after* the terminal event, not in the terminal event alone. **This is a claim about where boundary
evidence sits in time**, and its owner in our frame is the phrase-boundary primitive and L3's grouping,
not L1's cues. **Recorded, routed, not applied.**

**(5) A fourth instance of the ground-truth-bounds-the-figure pattern.** The authors exclude 25 of 270
annotated cadences because the annotation cannot be made to fit the analysis — 15 for a missing bass or
soprano, 10 for implying more than one category — and name the small sample for three of five categories
as a limit on generalisability. **Routed to measurement design**, beside rows 37 and 38's own versions of
the same point.

**(6) No falsifier.** Nothing read contradicts any CHOSEN design point. **No STOP fires** under the
remedial commission's §5.

## 4. What the record's decision points take from this paper, and what they do not — answered at the object

**No ratified text names this paper** (§6). So nothing in `FRAMEWORK.md` rests on it, and this section
places the paper against the decision points it bears on so that a later reader can see where it would
enter, not where it has.

**DP-B (tonality first, then chord? CHOSEN: no) and DP-E (tonality decided with the chords; a change
located at a harmonic boundary).** The paper decides tonality, chord and function TOGETHER in one dynamic
programme over the windowed graph, and locates a tonality change only where a cadence in the new tonality
is found. That is an instance of DP-B's chosen side and DP-E's, published in 2007 with hand-set weights and
NO measurement of the joint-versus-separate cost. It adds no figure to DP-B's ground (the measured
5-point and 2-point cost is another paper's) and it contradicts nothing. **What it adds is a worked
shape:** the tonality candidates are pre-filtered per window by an accidental test before the decode
(§2.3), so the joint decision runs over a tonality set already pruned by a hard diatonicity rule — a
pruning the record's own C36 argument (§4.2, *"a tonality model rating candidates by those tones rates
the true tonality lowest exactly where it is most strongly prolonged"*) does not touch, because the
paper's filter is a feasibility cut and not a rating.

**DP-C (segmentation before, with, or after chord identity? CHOSEN: with).** The paper is an instance of
DP-C's *"before (published; every fixed grid)"* rival: the bar is cut into windows at the shortest figure
duration before any harmonic decision, and the authors report the cost in their own words — chords
*"split by the windowing process"* that must be *"merged again"*, work they describe as ongoing. **It is
a published statement, by a system's own authors, that a fixed grid produces boundaries the harmony does
not have.** It carries no figure.

**DP-D (where does the chord-tone assignment live? CHOSEN: part of L2's one decision).** The paper's
melodic analysis is DP-D's excluded rival, *"an input, from an elaboration detector running first"* — with
one difference DP-D's candidate list does not describe: the detector runs first but leaves its CONFLICTS
undecided, and those are settled after the harmonic decision by membership in the decided chord (§2.6).
So the shape is *first-running detector with a post-decision resolution of its own ambiguities*. DP-D's
ground for exclusion — *"a first-running detector's mistakes are unrecoverable downstream"* — reaches
this shape for every note the detector tagged without conflict, whatever its confidence label, and does
not reach the notes it left in conflict. The paper reports no figure for its tagger (the F .72 at DP-D is another paper's). **Finding
(4) records this as an addition candidate to DP-D's rival record: a sub-shape, not a new candidate.**

**DP-I (cadence a layer, and on which side? CHOSEN: split — cues at L1, type at L3).** In the paper the
cadence is neither: it is INSIDE the joint decision, as the edge weights that make D→T progressions
dominate the path score and as the only licence for a tonality change. Table 4's cadence types are read
off the decided degrees, but their weight is applied during the decode. This is a third shape beside
DP-I's two rivals, *wholly upstream* and *wholly downstream*: cadence as a term of the joint objective.
The record's own §4.3 move 3 reads cadences off the decision and never revises it; the paper's cadence
both shapes the decision and is read off it. **No figure supports either side; it is recorded as a shape.**

**DP-K (what is published where it cannot decide? CHOSEN: rivals with mass).** The paper publishes one
best path and no rivals, with per-note confidence labels on the melodic tags only. An instance of
DP-K's excluded rival for the harmonic decision.

**DP-L (chord symbol a derivation? CHOSEN: yes).** Consistent: the chord is a set of note names decided
in the decode; no symbol is decided.

**DP-O (hierarchical reading? NONE CHOSEN).** **This paper is not evidence on DP-O's question as DP-O
states it.** It builds a
layered graph, not a tree; its edges connect successive windows only; no chord functions in two
tonalities at once; no grammar, no parse, no recursion. Its placement in the grammar group of the
proposed order (§0) is not a claim about its method and this read finds no ground for one. **DP-O stays
NONE CHOSEN and this row moves it nowhere.**

**DP-P (how are the terms of L2's score combined and fitted? NOT DECIDED HERE).** The paper's combination
is a sum of hand-set edge weights along a path, *"established empirically"*, with no procedure stated,
no held-out data and no fit — and its authors name learning the weights from a tagged corpus as future
work. It is the pre-fitting end of DP-P's question: a worked example of what the weights look like when
no one fits them (a D→T cadence at 1500–2500 against a T→S at 75), and of a design that carries its own
authors' statement that this is provisional.

**§4.2's entanglement (four questions, one decision).** The paper settles tonality, chord and function
together, and the chord-tone assignment HALF-together (§2.6). It does not settle the boundary with them:
the boundary is the fixed grid. So of the record's four entangled questions it takes three into one
decision and leaves one outside, and its own discussion reports the cost of leaving that one outside.

**D-335 (the function layer outputs the Roman numeral; T/S/D is a derived read-out, never a stored
output) and the D-586 paragraph.** The paper does the opposite of D-335: the tonal function is a NODE
LABEL decided in the decode, the degree is read off the chord's root, and Table 3's degree→function map
is many-valued (III → S, T, D), so the function is a decision and not a derivation there. This is the rival
D-335 excludes, with its ground at §2.4: the many-valued map is why the paper needs the decode to pick
the function. **Recorded beside D-335 as the published rival shape; applied nowhere.**

**D-337 (a lean toward another degree is a tonicization by default; a key change needs a confirming
cadence AND persistence).** The paper's *"tonality changes are allowed only when a cadence in a new
tonality is found"* is D-337's cadence half without its persistence half — and the authors report the
consequence: modulation points displaced by ±one chord, which they attribute to the dynamic programme.
**A published instance of the cadence-only rule and its stated cost.** Recorded beside D-337; applied
nowhere.

**D-527 (no live non-chord-tone cleaning stage; each tone emitted by category inside the one decode).**
The paper has the cleaning stage D-527 forbids, running first, rule-based, with a confidence per note.
The rival, published; no figure.

**D-023 (the atomic unit is the constant-sonority slice, never the metric beat).** The paper's unit is a
per-bar window at the shortest notated duration in that bar — neither the beat nor the slice: a grid the
paper presents as fine enough to hold every voice's notes, which coincides with the slice boundaries
wherever a change point falls on the grid, and which the authors' own compaction remark shows to cut
where the sonority does not change. Whether an onset can fall off that grid (a tuplet, say) is not
addressed by the paper and not derived here. A third unit beside D-023's two.

## ★ The placement question, DECIDED AT THE PAPER

The slice-derivation row (line 79) places row 40 in **L2's slice with an L3 bearing**, and says in
terms: *"What in it is L3's the row does not say; noted, not decided."* This is the answer, taken at the
paper and against the two charters read whole this session (`FRAMEWORK.md` §5, L2 at its heading and L3
at its heading, with the boundary contracts).

**The charters, quoted rather than paraphrased.** L2 publishes *"per span, the **tonality** as tonic and
mode"* and *"per span, the **chord** as degree, quality, figure and applied target, read against that
tonality"*. L3 publishes *"the **cadence** at each phrase end, with its type; the **phrase and section
grouping**; the **chord symbol** … the **figured bass**; the **harmonic rhythm**."* The boundary
contract L2 → L3 is forward-only and the contract L3 → L2 is **"Nothing."**

**The answer: the paper's own unit of record straddles the boundary, and it straddles it by
construction rather than by accident.** Its encoding token — *"III-IA3"* — carries, in one string and
in one annotating act, **(1) a local key area, which is L2's tonality per span; (2) a cadence
classification, which is L3's cadence type; and (3) the soprano's chord member at the arrival, which is
a read-off from a chord L2 decides.** The paper's central object, Tables 7 and 8 and the Figure 18
flowchart, is a **conditional distribution over the (key area, cadence type) PAIR given a melodic
fact** — the soprano's scale degree at the arrival and the interval leading into it, both of which are
L0/L1 facts about the notated melody.

**So what in it is L3's is the cadence-type half of every one of its labels, and what in it is L2's is
the local-key-area half — and the paper's finding is precisely about the pair, not about either half.**

**What this does NOT license, stated because the distance is short and the step would be wrong.** It is
**not** a refutation of DP-I / DP9's split (*cues at L1, type at L3*), and this read does not offer it
as one: that split is about where a cadence's TYPE is decided relative to the harmony, and a type read
off a decided harmony at L3 is entirely consistent with a corpus in which the composer chose key and
cadence together. What the paper bears on is **the evidence available to the L2 half** — whether the
tonality decision at a phrase ending can be taken well without the cadence-type question being open at
the same time. **That is a question this paper raises and does not answer**, because it never decides
anything: it records what Bach did, by hand, and tabulates it. **No claim is made here that the
framework's boundary is wrong**, and none should be read into this section.

**One further thing the paper settles about its own placement.** The paper's tonality is read **only at
fermata events**. It encodes nothing about the tonality between phrase endings, and it therefore says
nothing at all about a tonality change away from a cadence. **A reading that took this paper as
evidence FOR DP-E's clause that "a tonality change is located at a harmonic boundary" would be reading
the study's design as its result** — the design presupposes the reading is taken at the cadential
arrival, so it cannot test the clause. That is stated here so a later session does not make the step.

## What an L2 (or L3) detail specification could adopt, adapt, or must argue against

**What is NOT adoptable, said first because it bounds everything below — and said more carefully than
this extract's first writing said it, which the whole reading corrected.** There is **no score, no
term, no factor, no weight, no fitted parameter, no decoder, no segmentation procedure and no inference
over a score anywhere in the paper**, and the only code in it counts hand-made labels. **What there IS,
and what the first writing wrongly denied by calling the paper algorithm-free, is Figure 18: an
explicit hand-built decision flowchart** that maps a melodic condition to a predicted cadence and
carries a measured accounting rate. **It is a procedure, and it is not a fitted model, a search or an
inference** — its inputs (the soprano's degree at the arrival, the interval into it) are themselves
products of a hand annotation, and its branches were set by the author after inspecting the same
tables it is scored against.

**The annotation, stated at the right grain — the first writing over-reached by putting both passes at
the piano.** The **cadence categorization** was *"done by ear at the piano"* (page 195, the paper's own
words). The **melodic scale-degree encoding** was also by hand but is not described that way; what the
paper says of it is that non-harmonic tones *"had to be stripped away, which required some analytical
decisions"*, made *"on a case-by-case basis"* (page 193). Both are human judgments; only one is
described as made at an instrument.

**★ AND THE THING PRINCIPLE #20 REACHES, WHICH THIS EXTRACT'S FIRST WRITING DID NOT NAME.** The model
of Tables 7 and 8 is read off Tables 5 and 6, and Tables 5 and 6 are the whole corpus. **The 80.6% and
the 92.2% are therefore measured on exactly the data the model was derived from — no held-out split, no
cross-validation, no second corpus.** Under principle #20 (*"No value is graded on data that helped fit
it … A fitted-and-self-measured number is not established (#19)"*) **neither headline figure is an
established quantity in this project's sense**, and a specification citing either must carry that.
This is not an objection to the paper, which makes no out-of-sample claim; it is the bound under which
its figures may be used here.

**What IS adoptable or arguable, each named with what it would be used for:**

1. **Tables 7 and 8 as a PRIOR over (local key area, cadence type) at a phrase ending, conditioned on
   the soprano's scale degree.** The L2 charter leaves to the detail specification *"how the score over
   candidate readings is formed, what its terms are, what tables they read"*. This is a published,
   on-repertoire table of exactly that shape — three cadence types over five key areas in each of the
   two tables — with counts behind every cell (Tables 5 and 6) and a **self-measured** success rate for
   the reduction (claims 8 and 9, under the principle-#20 bound stated above). A specification adding a
   phrase-ending term would cite it or argue against it.
2. **The Figure 18 flowchart as a stated decision procedure with a measured accounting rate (92.2%).**
   Adoptable as a baseline to beat, or as the shape of a rival a specification must exclude.
3. **The fermata-to-arrival displacement rule (claim 12) against the phrase-boundary primitive.** The
   record's D-481 rules that *"The notated markers are emitted as boundaries unconditionally; only the
   surface-cue strength is peak-picked"*, and D-477 that phrase boundaries are read from the written
   surface alone. **This paper states, on this repertoire, that the harmonic arrival is systematically
   displaced from the notated fermata under a stated melodic condition.** A specification that emits the
   fermata as the boundary and expects the harmonic arrival there would have to carry this.
4. **The "NC" category as a named published instance of DP-Q's open question.** DP-Q reads *"Some
   published schemas carry a no-chord label and a no-cadence verdict; the three exemplar analyses
   contain neither"* — and names none. **This is such a schema, held, on this repertoire, with the
   verdict's frequency measured (1.1% in Table 3, 1.3% in Table 4).**
5. **The subdominant stop as an argument that the standard cadence vocabulary is incomplete for this
   repertoire**, with a measured frequency (2.7% of fermata events) and a significance test for its
   key-dependence. L3's charter publishes *"the cadence at each phrase end, with its type"* and
   enumerates no type vocabulary; this is an argument about what that vocabulary must contain.
6. **The two-annotator agreement figure and its named disagreement class**, against principle #21 and
   against D-337. See the findings below.

## Bearing on the framework — flagged, not decided (verdicts belong to Task 4)

**Read against `FRAMEWORK.md` §9 (DP-O) and §11 (R-7), both read at the file this session.**

**★ R-7's THIRD NAMED UNREAD ALTERNATIVE IS NOW READ.** R-7 names three: *"a tonality estimated at
every window size at once"* (row 17, Sapp — read), *"a time-span reduction tree"* (**this row**), and
*"tonality in a transform space rather than as a discrete label"* (row 18, Wavescapes — read).
**With this chapter, all three are read at a primary.** Whether that discharges R-7 is Task 4's; what
is established is that the reading gap R-7 names is closed.

**DP-O — this row supplies NEITHER support NOR a falsifier, and the reason is sharper than "no
measurement".** DP-O asks whether the framework commits to *a hierarchical reading of harmony*, and
names its falsifier as *a tree model beating a matched-capacity sequence model on this repertoire's
ground truth*. This chapter:

1. **does not model harmony hierarchically at all** — the prolongational reduction, the subtheory that
   *"explicitly indicat[es] harmonic retention and change"*, **is the one it did not implement** (p. 209);
2. **is monophonic**, where this project's repertoire is four-voice chorales;
3. **reports no comparison against any sequence model**, matched-capacity or otherwise;
4. and its trees are **reductions of a melody**, graded against expert GTTM annotations — a different
   object and a different ground truth from DP-O's.

**So DP-O stays open exactly as it was, and this row cannot move it.** *NOT claimed:* that no GTTM-line
paper could bear on DP-O; the prolongational analyzer was *"being developed"* in 2013 and later work in
the line (σGTTM, deepGTTM) is unread here.

**★ WHAT THE ROW DOES CONTRIBUTE, AND IT IS NOT NOTHING — two facts about the shape of the problem.**

- **The dependency direction.** The best-developed time-span-reduction implementation puts its
  hierarchy **downstream of tonality and harmony**, needs region and chord distances to run its most
  consequential grouping rule, and **does not compute them**. Any future proposal that hierarchy should
  inform the tonal reading meets this as evidence about the direction the one working implementation
  had to take.
- **The cost of executing a hierarchical theory.** A celebrated theory required **46 parameters** —
  a third of them admitted to *"lack clear musicological meaning"* — introduced by iterating against
  results already considered correct, and still reaches **F ≈ 0.49 automatically** on monophonic
  eight-bar excerpts. **That is a measured statement about tractability**, and it is the same shape as
  HarmTrace's parse-space finding (row 5) from a different direction: a rich hierarchical formalism
  becomes runnable by having something taken out of it or bolted onto it.

**L3 grouping (the framework's read-off facts) — one item worth routing.** The metrical-structure
analyzer scores **0.84 at default parameters**, against grouping's 0.46. Metrical structure is, on this
evidence, much the more mechanically recoverable of the two. Read beside V5's finding that removing
metrical-accent features costs about six points of F-measure in a segmental analyser, it is
consistent — the metrical layer is both recoverable and useful — but **these are different corpora,
different objects and different metrics, and no arithmetic joins them.**

**NO FALSIFIER CANDIDATE against any chosen design point.** Every point this row touches — DP-O — is
underived and open, so nothing here is a STOP under the commission's §6.
